functionalObligations.text: orders are matched in a central limit order book by a purpose-built Go microservice matching engine that operates independently of on-chain block times
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE — Ob asserts an ON-CHAIN order book, and the venue says in its own words that the engine runs off chain. The symbol is right about the microstructure and false about the qualifier, exactly as the corpus marker records.

functionalObligations.text: matching runs in an operator-run engine and only state roots are anchored to Ethereum, with the operator as sole block proposer
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE — matching locus. Same Ob as Hyperliquid's in-consensus book and Lighter's proven book; three trust models, one symbol. V2 architecture claim corroborated at https://edgex-1.gitbook.io/edgeX-documentation/edgex-v2.md (2026-08-04).

functionalObligations.text: the venue has occupied two different loci while keeping the product, the account model and the API shape: V1 was 'powered by the StarkEx Layer 2 engine' as a validium, and V2 is a modular rollup that has 'temporarily adopted the Arbitrum technology stack as a transitional framework', with V3 announced as a sovereign AppChain
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and a DEPARTURE from the corpus, whose entire edgeX record describes the legacy StarkEx generation. A vocabulary blind to the locus cannot detect that a venue's failure mode changed underneath its users. Nothing in the framework has a notion of a venue persisting across an architecture change. EDGE Chain announced as 'an app-specific rollup powered by Arbitrum' at https://blog.arbitrum.io/edgex-announces-edge-chain-on-arbitrum/ (dated 2026-03-10, accessed 2026-08-04).

functionalObligations.text: no constraint on the operator's ordering, matching or inclusion discretion is published for either generation: there is no fairness rule, no sequencing commitment and no forced-ordering property, and the Cairo program that executed V1's state transitions is marked 'Code unknown'

V1 batched trades through the StarkEx service to the SHARP shared prover, whose STARK proofs were verified on Ethereum before the StarkPerpetual contract would accept a state root; for V2 the documentation never states whether there are validity proofs, fault proofs, or neither
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE — proof system, and stage 1's judgement that this is the single most consequential unstated fact about the venue. The 58 have no element for a proof, so they can record neither the V1 regime nor V2's silence about it. StarkPerpetual 0xfAaE2946e846133af314d1Df13684c89fA7d83DD (https://l2beat.com/scaling/projects/edgex, 2026-08-04).

functionalObligations.text: V1 is a validium: proof construction relies fully on data that is not published on chain, held by a data-availability committee with a threshold of 2 of 6 whose members are not publicly known and who have no on-chain assets at risk of being slashed in a data-withholding attack; V2's data-availability regime is not stated
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE — data availability. Nothing separates a validium from a rollup, which is the whole liveness and exit risk of the venue; and the quantitative version is what makes it live — the threshold is a number, it is 2 of 6, the members are anonymous and the stake at risk is zero. FinalizableCommittee 0x23bf3dcc14680162b7f5355aAbb56D31823c946e.

functionalObligations.text: on V1 a user may force the sequencer to include a trade or a withdrawal by submitting the request through L1, and if it is censored or down for 7 days anyone may freeze the system and withdraw by Merkle proof — but a forced TRADE requires the user to find a counterparty by out-of-system means; V2 asserts trustless permissionless withdrawals at any time even under operator sequence failure while specifying no mechanism, no deadline and no contract
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE — exit. Two unnameable things: an exit right whose exercise is conditioned on the user's own market access (find a counterparty out of band), and an exit CLAIM with no mechanism behind it. Compare Lighter, where order creation itself is forceable. Deadline and freeze mechanics from https://l2beat.com/scaling/projects/edgex (2026-08-04).

functionalObligations.text: USDT is deposited from Ethereum mainnet after roughly 15 confirmations (about 5 minutes) and credited to the trader's L2 account

a deposit from a non-Ethereum chain is credited by transferring an equivalent amount from the venue's own asset pool on that chain, with rebalancing latency of up to 2 hours for single deposits over $300K
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the reason `Xm` is DROPPED from the corpus element set. This is not cross-domain message verification: it is a market-maker inventory standing in for a bridge, with its own solvency question and its own rebalancing risk. Xf covers the Ethereum path (F8) and nothing covers this one.

functionalObligations.text: a user may onboard by email, in which case an MPC wallet is created for them and a fresh address is funded over Arbitrum
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Au (delegated execution scope) is the nearest symbol and is the wrong direction: the venue co-holds a share of the user's signing key rather than receiving a bounded authority from the user. A custody arrangement dressed as an account is not expressible.

functionalObligations.text: the account is cross-margined so that collateral is shared among all positions within one trading account, isolation is obtained by opening separate sub-accounts, and sub-account volume aggregates into the main account's fee tier
functionalObligations.note: Ct computes the test; margin scope is unnameable here as everywhere in the category. The fee-tier aggregation across nominally isolated sub-accounts — a coupling between risk fences — has no symbol either.

functionalObligations.text: risk is parameterised per contract by a 22-step notional staircase published as API metadata rather than as protocol constants: for BTCUSDT tier 1 covers notional up to $50,000 at 100x with a maintenance-margin rate of 0.5%, rising to a top tier at 6x and 10.5%
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE — the explicit initial-margin and maintenance-margin FORMULAS are not published anywhere, so Ct is discharged by a table of parameters with no stated computation over them. A risk parameter that is API data rather than a protocol constant is also a control-plane fact — the operator can restate it without an upgrade — that no element carries.

functionalObligations.text: the Index Price is a weighted average of prices collected from Binance, OKX, Bybit and Coinbase with weights readjusted every four hours, and it drives funding
functionalObligations.note: Ex fits: genuinely external publishers, unlike Hyperliquid's and Aster's validator-produced prices. V2 additionally claims a native Multi-CEX oracle aggregation pipeline (https://edgex-1.gitbook.io/edgeX-documentation/edgex-v2.md, 2026-08-04). Tp is NOT claimed — the weighting is across venues, not across time.

functionalObligations.text: a second and different price, the Oracle Price sourced from the independent provider Stork, drives margin requirements and liquidation prices
functionalObligations.note: One symbol, two feeds, two jobs, two failure modes: nothing in the vocabulary says WHICH obligation a given price discharges, so a venue that funds off one publisher and liquidates off another decomposes identically to one that uses a single feed for both.

functionalObligations.text: longs and shorts exchange funding hourly at F = P + clamp(I - P, -0.05%, +0.05%) with P = [max(0, ImpactBid - Index) - max(0, Index - ImpactAsk)] / Index, longs paying shorts when the rate is positive
functionalObligations.note: Pf fits exactly — a genuine long/short transfer, so the category's 'perp tether' flag is refuted here as it is for the other four.

functionalObligations.text: in cross mode a position is liquidated when the available balance reaches zero and the position margin drops to the maintenance-margin level
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE — the page states the TRIGGER and nothing else. Whether a third party is paid to close the position, at what price, in what order, and with what fee is undocumented, so the 'incentivized' half of Li is unsupported rather than merely absent. Li is retained only because a forced close demonstrably occurs; it is the sole loss-handling element this venue's documentation supports, and stage 3 should treat that as fragile.

functionalObligations.text: what absorbs a bankrupt position is not documented: the strings 'insurance fund', 'auto-deleveraging', 'bankruptcy price', 'socialised loss' and any liquidation-fee schedule are absent from the venue's entire 414 KB documentation corpus
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the reason `Bs` is DROPPED from the corpus element set — its justification ('insurance fund is non-slashable protocol capital') describes a fund that is nowhere asserted. `Sl` and `Ad` are likewise NOT claimed, for the same reason. The deeper finding: the vocabulary has a symbol for each candidate answer (Bs, Sl, Ad) and no way to record that NONE is asserted, so the honest decomposition of a venue running at scale with an unstated loss-absorption layer is indistinguishable from an incomplete one.

functionalObligations.text: critical contracts can be upgraded by an externally owned account, with no delay and no window for users to exit an unwanted upgrade, while the bridge contract itself is immutable and its committee security 'cannot be improved'
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE, and the strongest control-plane fact in the category. Up names a mutable implementation proxy and carries no delay parameter and no authority type, so it cannot say 'a single key, instantly, with no exit window' — which is L2BEAT's headline risk. `Tg` and `Gp` are deliberately NOT claimed (the corpus asserts Gp): the upgrading Safe 0x57814cC6e075f517781cB7c3B42897B3Bb2C54d8 'can upgrade with no delay', only the SHARP multisig 0x21F9eC47b19d95b5C2DDFB6Ae5D4F92fAdacAEc4 carries an 8-day delay, and no product-side guardian, pause or governance vote is documented. If the tables require a delayed or bounded emergency process alongside Up, this construction fails that requirement, and the failure is the finding. `Sh` and `Em` are DROPPED for the same evidentiary reason: no pro-rata pool, vault or LP claim is documented anywhere in the venue's corpus, and no emissions schedule is documented at a primary source — the EDGE token TGE and the Amber Group incubation appear only in third-party coverage and are recorded as UNKNOWN (https://edgex-1.gitbook.io/edgeX-documentation/llms-full.txt, 2026-08-04).

paper.title: edgeX
paper.label: cat:perp:edgex
paper.blurb: A venue in the middle of a migration: a validity-proof stack still holds real value at almost no throughput while a rollup serves current activity. Which stack custodies a new deposit is not stated in its documentation, and the question is not one the vocabulary can put.
paper.witnessReason: The witness is deliberately thin. The corpus carries a staked backstop, a cross-domain verification element, a share claim and emissions; none is supported at a primary source for the current system, so all four are dropped. What remains is what can be evidenced, and the construction is rejected because of it.
paper.residueNote: The rejection is a result about the tables and not a criticism of the venue: the requirement demands a named loss-absorption mechanism, and this venue documents none. An undocumented mechanism and an absent one are different things, and the vocabulary cannot tell them apart --- which is the same defect the options category exhibits from the other side.
